function: Deep RL (FPDS-DDPG) jointly chooses LEO beam radius and per-beam transmit power to maximize LEO spectral efficiency under GEO interference, power and Doppler-offset constraints (p. 6-7)
system: GEO-LEO coexisting satellites, multi-beam LEO phased array, single-antenna GEO and LEO users, no RIS, L-band 1.53 GHz, LEO altitude 785 km (p. 3, p. 10)
method: Deep RL: FPDS-DDPG, a DDPG actor-critic with post-decision state and fuzzy-logic exploration; trained offline in a simulator, 2000 episodes, continuous actions (p. 7-10)
data_channel: Custom MATLAB Satellite Toolbox simulator: Shadowed-Rician fading {m,b,w}={4,0.126,0.835}, free-space path loss, Doppler offsets from Iridium-NEXT 914 orbital data; no 3GPP model or measurements (p. 4, p. 10)
test_conditions: Learning curves in Table II simulator with {m,b,w}={4,0.126,0.835}; robustness test over three Shadowed-Rician scenarios (m=10.1, 19.4, 0.739); reuse and handover cases (p. 10-13)
baselines: Learned: DDPG [16], DPDS-DPG [21] (authors' earlier method). Non-learned: beam size by elevation angle [26], beam size with Doppler offset [27], power control [28] (p. 7, 13)
metrics: LEO spectral efficiency, SINR at GEO and LEO users, interference power, average reward per episode, robustness score, GEO-protection violations, episodes to converge (p. 11-13)
complexity: Big-O orders for training and online operation (Table I, p. 10); 123904 FLOPs per forward pass, 2.48 µs on CPU, 0.248 µs on DPU (p. 14)
q1_support: p. 10: "generated using Shadowed-Rician fading with parameters" {m,b,w}={4,0.126,0.835} from [21]; Doppler from orbital data. Missing: any 3GPP TR 38.811 model or measured channel data; 3GPP is cited only for frequency reuse (p. 2).
q2_support: p. 11: "we evaluate its performance across three distinct satellite downlink channel conditions" (m=10.1, 19.4, 0.739) versus m=4 in the simulator setup (p. 10); p. 9: "generalization to unseen conditions". Retraining per scenario is not mentioned.
q3_support: p. 13: "we compare its performance against three nonlearning benchmarks", Benchmark 3 giving "a 24.25% reduction in spectral efficiency"; p. 11, Table IV compares DDPG [16] and DPDS-DPG [21] on average reward, which p. 9 defines as measuring long-term performance.
q4_support: p. 14: "123904 FLOPs" for a forward pass of actor and critic, "processing time is 2.48 µs" on a 50 GFLOPS CPU; Table I (p. 10) lists the big-O complexity of training and online operation.
q5_support: p. 10: "CSN environment simulator is implemented using MATLAB" Satellite Toolbox and PyTorch; channels are generated randomly. Missing: any link to code or data, and any public channel dataset or measured data.
notes: NTN area 6: the learned element is LEO beam size and power control. q1: Shadowed-Rician with parameters from Abdi et al. [25] is a statistical fading model, not 3GPP TR 38.811, so 0. q2 borderline: the robustness test (p. 9, p. 11) uses channel parameters different from the training setup, but the paper never says whether the agent was retrained per scenario. q3 borderline: learned baselines are mostly compared on convergence speed (Figs. 4-5, p. 11), yet Table IV also gives average reward, equal to spectral efficiency when constraints hold (eq. 23, p. 7); DPDS-DPG is the authors' earlier method that FPDS-DDPG extends with fuzzy exploration, and DDPG is the standard algorithm on the same problem. Tables I-IV and Figs. 4-5, 9-12 were read as page images (p. 10, 11, 13).
